channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Huawei Set to Unveil China’s Best Answer to Nvidia AI Chip Reign
item.description: Huawei Technologies Co. is set to unveil new AI technology this week in defiance of US export control curbs, advancing its ambition to replace Nvidia Corp. in China and compete on the global stage.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Salesforce Sees $63 Billion in Revenue in Fiscal Year 2030
item.description: Salesforce Inc. gave a long-term outlook for sales that exceeded analysts’ estimates, signaling to investors that the software company can boost revenue growth in the face of competition from artificial intelligence tools.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: OpenAI Reports New AI Safety Incidents, Sets Disclosure Process
item.description: OpenAI shared several undisclosed incidents of its artificial intelligence models misbehaving, and unveiled a new framework for how it plans to track and disclose such incidents going forward.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Apple’s Cook, OpenAI CEO to Attend Trump Dinner With Xi
item.description: Apple Inc. Executive Chairman Tim Cook and OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman are poised to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping next week.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary and Mark Gurman

item.title: AI Doom Hits Tech World
item.description: Bloomberg Odd Lots hosts Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway react to AI skepticism and recent warnings coming from people in the industry. The pair discuss what the hacking of Hugging Face might tell us about where AI is headed and what some of the biggest risks of these warnings could be, arguing "when everything is couched in these existential terms, you end up just getting a race right to who can develop first." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Tracking Cyber Threats Against Nearly 20 Ships Worldwide
item.description: US government agencies are tracking cyber threats against nearly 20 shipping vessels around the world, according to US officials familiar with the situation.
item.dc:creator: Jake Bleiberg, Myles Miller and Ryan Gallagher

item.title: Fed Hikes Rates for the First Time Since 2023
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are DoubleLine Capital Portfolio Manager Ken Shinoda, Brookings President Cecilia Rouse, Hoover Institution Senior Fellow Michael Spence, OMFIF Chief Economist, Vice Chair Mark Sobel, BlackRock Global Head of Retirement Solutions Nick Nefouse, & Brown Harris Stevens CEO Bess Freedman. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DoubleLine’s Shinoda: I Think the 10-Year Goes Higher
item.description: Ken Shinoda of DoubleLine Capital said the Fed’s unanimous rate hike was largely in line with market expectations, noting that traders had already priced in a better-than-90% chance of a move. He pointed to the reaction in Treasuries as evidence that the market believes more tightening may still be needed, with the 10-year yield slightly higher on the day and the long bond giving back some of its initial rally. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI’s Brockman on Developing AI in the Wake of Hugging Face
item.description:
According to OpenAI President Greg Brockman, it was no surprise to the company that some of its models were able to break free of the testing environment — but what's happened since has forced some rethinking.
Brockman joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss what OpenAI has learned since the Hugging Face hacking incident and how worried we should be about the AI doomsday scenarios. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Drone Startup Zipline in Talks on About $1 Billion Raise at $20 Billion Valuation
item.description: Zipline is in talks to raise around $1 billion in a funding round that would value the drone delivery and logistics startup at roughly $20 billion, nearly tripling its previous valuation.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas, Edward Ludlow and Hema Parmar

item.title: Banks Line Up $22 Billion Chip Loan Tied to Blackstone, Alphabet
item.description: A group of 10 banks is providing a $22 billion chip loan to support Blackstone Inc. and Alphabet Inc.’s new cloud venture Crux AI, the latest mega-debt deal in the race to finance the expensive processors crucial to artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Paula Seligson, Preeti Singh and Michelle Cheng

item.title: Status Of Anthropic IPO As AI Fears Mount
item.description: Bloomberg's Anthony Hughes joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Anthropic is preparing for its IPO and has picked Nasdaq as its listing venue. The Claude chatbot maker is seeking to raise as much as or more than SpaceX in an IPO that could take place as soon as October, Bloomberg has reported. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zuckerberg, Huang Break With Industry Leaders on AI Warnings
item.description: Bloomberg's Mike Shepard said President Trump's opposition to AI guardrails is another instance of his anti-regulation position across all industries, as well as his closeness with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang who recently pushed back on fears about AI safety. Shepard said that President Trump is also looking to his meeting with China's President Xi and wants no obstacles around AI heading into that conversation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Is 'Huge Factor' In Success of US Economy, Says Stephen Moore
item.description: Stephen Moore, former senior economic adviser to President Donald Trump said that the AI industry is a 'huge factor' in the US economy given both the investment pouring into the space and the data center construction boom. Moore also discussed high oil and diesel prices, saying that as the price of energy rises so does 'everything else.' Despite high energy prices, Moore says he's bullish on the outlook for the US economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bain Capital Ventures Bets $1.6 Billion on AI’s Next Act
item.description: Bain Capital Ventures has raised a $1.6 billion fund to back early-stage companies built for what it calls “life after AGI.” Partner Slater Stich discusses where the firm sees opportunities across AI infrastructure, software, robotics and science, why knowledge work could be transformed first, and how BCV identifies founders capable of building the next generation of category-defining AI companies. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Safety Talks Stir Startup Concerns
item.description: AI startups are growing concerned that calls from Anthropic and OpenAI to “pace” frontier development could lead to a new regulatory framework shaped by the industry’s biggest players. Bloomberg’s Natasha Mascarenhas and Maggie Eastland discuss the reaction from founders and investors and early talks among OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind on common safety standards. Also being debated in Washington is if those efforts require government involvement or changes to antitrust rules. They join Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta CEO Weighs In on AI Safety Debate
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Mark Zuckerberg's call for AI labs to rely on independent evaluators and advisers to ensure models are safe. Plus, OpenAI is said to be in early talks with investors about a new funding round that could value the ChatGPT maker at more than $1.2 trillion, and Impulse Space CEO Tom Mueller discusses the company's $308 million Series D extension and the future of the space mobility economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The AI Industry Says It Wants To Slow Down. Can It?
item.description: On today’s Big Take podcast, Sarah Holder and Bloomberg tech editor Sarah Frier break down the many reasons and motivations behind AI leaders’ calls to slow the development of so-called frontier models. What are they asking of the US government, and how much could they do to “pace the frontier” on their own? Listen wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Looking to Raise More Money Ahead of Public Debut
item.description: OpenAI is holding early talks with investors about a fresh funding round that would value the ChatGPT creator at more than $1.2 trillion ahead of an initial public offering. Bloomberg's Shirin Ghaffary joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Rate Hike Looms as Retail Sales Surge
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Isabelle Lee and Damian Sassower on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Markets brace for the Fed, with its first rate hike since 2023 widely expected. Retail sales surge as US consumers keep spending. Plus, Meta pushes AI oversight as OpenAI eyes a $1.2 trillion valuation. And Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire joins us on why he still believes the Clarity Act could become law even though it failed to pass the US Senate. (Source: Bloomberg)
